chunks: He said: “When the last ten days arrived, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform i'tikaf in the mosque, and a tent of hair would be set up for him, and he would tighten the waist-wrapper, and fold up his bedding.”
And some of them said: “And he kept away from women.”
So Abū ʿAbdِ ٱللَّهِ عليه السلام said: “As for keeping away from women, no.”

key_terms.شَعْرٍ: hair, indicating the material from which the tent was made
key_terms.شَمَّرَ ٱلْمِئْزَرَ: he tightened the waist-wrapper, an expression indicating readiness and seriousness
key_terms.فِرَاشَهُ: his bedding, which he folded away
key_terms.قُبَّةٌ: a tent or canopy set up for privacy and seclusion
key_terms.ٱعْتَكَفَ: he performed i'tikaf, meaning spiritual retreat in the mosque
key_terms.ٱعْتِزَالُ ٱلنِّسَاءِ: keeping away from women, which is negated here as part of the reported practice
key_terms.ٱلْعَشْرُ ٱلْأَوَاخِرُ: the last ten days, referring to the final ten days of a sacred period
key_terms.ٱلْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the place where the retreat was observed

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم do during the last ten days of retreat, and did i'tikaf require avoiding women?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم during the last ten days, emphasizing i'tikaf in the mosque and outward signs of devotion and preparation. It also clarifies, through Abū ʿAbdِ ٱللَّهِ عليه السلام, that the claim that he would avoid women in this context is not accepted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2087 - It is narrated:
"When the last ten nights of Month of Ramadan arrived, the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) would perform i'tikaf in the mosque. A tent made of hair would be set up for him, he would tighten his waist wrap, and he would fold up his bedding."
Some people said he would also avoid the company of women.
Regarding this, Abu Abdullah (as) said: "As for avoiding women, no."
